answers.name: Emerald
answers.fact: A green beryl, almost always with inclusions.

answers.name: Pearl
answers.fact: The only gem made by a living animal.

answers.name: Amethyst
answers.fact: The Greeks thought it prevented drunkenness.

answers.name: Opal
answers.fact: Australia mines about 95% of the world's opal.

answers.name: Jade
answers.fact: Actually two different minerals: jadeite and nephrite.

answers.name: Aquamarine
answers.fact: A blue-green beryl, named for seawater.

answers.name: Turquoise
answers.fact: Prized by the ancient Egyptians and the Aztecs.

answers.name: Lapis lazuli
answers.fact: Ground up to make ultramarine paint.

answers.name: Tanzanite
answers.fact: Found in only one place, near Mount Kilimanjaro.

answers.name: Tourmaline
answers.fact: Comes in more colours than any other gem.

answers.name: Amber
answers.fact: Fossilised tree resin, sometimes with insects inside.

answers.name: Quartz
answers.fact: The second most common mineral on Earth's crust.

answers.name: Zircon
answers.fact: Some zircons are the oldest minerals on Earth, at 4.4 billion years.

answers.name: Spinel
answers.fact: The 'Black Prince's Ruby' in the British crown is actually spinel.

answers.name: Tiger's eye
answers.fact: Shows a shimmering band of light.

answers.name: Alexandrite
answers.fact: Changes colour between daylight and lamplight.

answers.name: Morganite
answers.fact: A pink beryl, named after banker J.P. Morgan.

answers.name: Hematite
answers.fact: An iron ore polished into dark gems.

answers.name: Rhodochrosite
answers.fact: Pink banded mineral, Argentina's national gem.

answers.name: Moissanite
answers.fact: First found in a meteor crater, now mostly lab-made.

answers.name: Fluorite
answers.fact: Glows under ultraviolet light; gave us the word 'fluorescence'.

answers.name: Chrysoprase
answers.fact: An apple-green chalcedony, mined in Queensland.

answers.name: Smoky quartz
answers.fact: A brown-grey quartz; Scotland's national gem.

answers.name: Taaffeite
answers.fact: Found already cut, in a jeweller's lot, in 1945.

answers.name: Painite
answers.fact: Once called the rarest mineral on Earth.

answers.name: Larimar
answers.fact: A sky-blue stone from the Dominican Republic.

answers.name: Sugilite
answers.fact: A purple stone from Japan and South Africa.

answers.name: Andalusite
answers.fact: Flashes different colours from different angles.

answers.name: Kyanite
answers.fact: Has different hardness in different directions.

answers.name: Apatite
answers.fact: Often mistaken for other gems; its name means 'deceit'.

answers.name: Danburite
answers.fact: A clear stone first found in Connecticut.

answers.name: Moldavite
answers.fact: A green glass formed by a meteor impact.

answers.name: Musgravite
answers.fact: A rare gem named after the Musgrave Ranges of South Australia.

answers.name: Grandidierite
answers.fact: A blue-green gem first found in Madagascar.

answers.name: Poudretteite
answers.fact: A pink gem first found in a Quebec quarry.

answers.name: Black opal
answers.fact: Lightning Ridge in NSW is famous for it.

answers.name: Thunder egg
answers.fact: A plain rock that cracks open to show agate or opal inside.
